questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Negating one whole clause with a single word
questions.learningObjective: Negate a clause in a table row
questions.stem: Explain how to negate 'El grafico es claro' in one step.

answer.exemplar: Insert no before the verb to produce 'El grafico no es claro,' which negates the whole clause with a single negative word.

questions.explanation: A single no before the verb negates the entire clause. Placing it elsewhere would not negate the statement correctly.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The correlative pair ni and ni
questions.learningObjective: Explain the structure of ni...ni
questions.stem: Explain the structure of the ni...ni pair in a negative clause.

answer.exemplar: The ni...ni pair places ni before each of two or more items after a leading no, so all items share one negation in a neither-nor structure.

questions.explanation: ni precedes each item and a leading no negates the whole list. Missing a ni or the leading no breaks the structure.
questions.hint: no plus ni before each item.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Where the word no sits in a Spanish clause
questions.learningObjective: State where no goes with a compound tense
questions.stem: Explain where no goes in a compound tense such as 'he comido'.

answer.exemplar: In a compound tense, no goes before the auxiliary verb, as in 'No he comido,' so the whole clause is negated before the participle appears.

questions.explanation: no precedes the auxiliary in compound tenses. Placing it after the auxiliary or before the participle breaks the standard order.
